newsitem.title: USA: Excel takes Q1 after-tax charge of $65 mln.
newsitem.headline: Excel takes Q1 after-tax charge of $65 mln.

text.p: EXCEL Communications Inc said Monday that it will recognize a one-time charge of $65 million, or $0.59 a share, in the first quarter of 1997 to reflect a change in accounting practice.

The company said it is changing its accounting for customer acquisition costs effective January 1. Previously, EXCEL said it had deferred the portions of commissions paid to independent representatives that directly relate to the acquisition of long distance subscribers. Beginning January 1, the Company will be fully expensing customer acquisition costs in the period incurred.
EXECEL said it has consistently disclosed the effect of the deferral on results since its initial public offering.
The company said it is changing its accounting practice in order to present its operating results in a manner more consistent with its peers.
EXCEL is the fifth largest long distance company in the United States in terms of presubscribed lines according to the Federal Communications Commission.
